sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Alisanos, also Alisanus, is an obscure Continental Celtic god of the Gauls. His name may have been given to the great settlement of Alesia. The name is read in different ways: as stone, as alder, or as rowan. Koch derives the second element from the alder tree. Alesia was a Celtic oppidum, the capital of the Mandubii in Burgundy, and the site of the last fight between the Gauls and the Romans in 52 BC.
